items.title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke
items.author: Peiying Li
items.content: The serotonin receptor Htr2b activation enhances lysosome biogenesis and phagocytic clearance of debris to mitigate neuroinflammation and brain injury after stroke. The study proposes a potential monocyte-derived macrophage-targeted immune therapy to improve neurological outcomes after ischemic stroke.

items.title: Circuit mechanisms for disentangled representations and generalization in the hippocampus
items.author: Antonio Fernandez-Ruiz
items.content: The hippocampus encodes different aspects of experience as disentangled variables, enabling flexible recombination and generalization to new situations. This code is supported by the geometry of population dynamics and cell–assembly interactions.

items.title: Stimulus-specific recruitment of human amygdala neurons predicts episodic memory encoding success
items.author: Ueli Rutishauser
items.content: The study shows that stimulus-specific neurons in the human amygdala determine which experiences become lasting memory, revealing a mechanism that predicts episodic memory formation and may guide future treatments for memory disorders.

items.title: Microglial NUS1 deficiency drives dopaminergic neurodegeneration through intercellular iron dysregulation in Parkinson’s disease models
items.author: Haigang Ren
items.content: Using cellular and mouse models, this study reports that deficiency of the Parkinson’s disease risk gene NUS1 in microglia disrupts intercellular iron homeostasis, leading to neuronal iron overload and dopaminergic neurodegeneration.

items.title: Chronic progressive demyelination induces a microglial state with lysosomal dysfunction
items.author: Mikael Simons
items.content: Acute myelin injury responses are well defined, but microglia adaptations to chronic damage remain unclear. Mouse models reveal a chronic demyelination-associated microglial state marked by inflammation, lysosomal dysfunction and myelin-damaging activity.

items.title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT<sub>2A</sub>R–β-arrestin signaling
items.author: Sheng Wang
items.content: This study shows that the sustained antidepressant-like effect of psychedelics is driven by 5-HT2A receptor–β-arrestin signaling. Repeated low-dose LSD preserves this effect in mice without inducing hallucinogenic-like behaviors in mice or monkeys.

items.title: Identification of candidate markers for the isolation of neuron-specific extracellular vesicles
items.author: David R. Walt
items.content: The authors developed methods to identify extracellular vesicles (EVs) in the blood that come from the brain by capturing EV surface proteins. This could be used in the future to diagnose neurological diseases.

items.title: Network geometry shapes the transformation of task representations across the human cortex
items.author: Michael W. Cole
items.content: The dimensionality of intrinsic brain connectivity systematically shapes how task representations compress and expand across the cortex, and activity flow modeling shows the active role of network geometry in generating the transformation.
